newsitem.title: INDIA: Gloom stays as Indian stocks pause to catch breath.
newsitem.headline: Gloom stays as Indian stocks pause to catch breath.

text.p: Indian shares paused to catch their breath on Monday after hopes of a market reforms package were dashed last week, leaving stunned speculators uncertain about their next move, analysts said.
But they said the mood could turn upbeat in the run-up to the country's federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) due on February 28.
"Everyone's disappointed and frustrated with the market. The speculators have all gone quiet," said the chief dealer at a London-based broking firm.

Bombay's benchmark stocks index fell 58.25 points, or 1.72 percent, to close at 3324.22 in low volumes. Traders said there was some late selling by speculators but investors remained on the sidelines.
The Delhi stocks index closed 18.59 points, or 2.5 percent, lower at 713.06. On the Bombay-based National Stock Exchange, the index dropped 24.45 points, or 2.5 percent, to 948.20.

"Right now it's not interesting to commit one way or another and that's why it's so quiet. There's no real confidence to sell at this level as investors expect a little rally before the budget," the chief dealer said.
Share prices rose sharply in January on frequent assurances by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda that his government would unveil a series of new market-friendly policy initiaties.
But Finance Minister P. Chidambaram dashed hopes last week when he said the expected package actually consisted of measures already taken since January.

Bombay's index reacted sharply, plunging 127.58 points, or 3.6 percent, to 3382.47 on Friday -- losing 1.5 percent in the week. Most analysts said they were advising investors to pick up selected stocks if prices fell by another 100-150 points.
"The mood now is to only look for specific good stock ideas," said Alok Sethi, director at Natwest Securities.
The head of sales at a European brokerage said though investors were unsure what turn the market would take, they were likely to pick cyclicals such as commodity stocks at lower levels.
"Everyone's looking at cyclicals more closely," he said.
Commodity stocks have been in the doldrums during most of the past year on a slowdown in demand and weak global prices.
"The cycles are turning for the better and it's a good defensive strategy. There's interest in aluminium, steel and petrochemical stocks," he said.
In a note to investors, Khandwala Securities said the trend was likely to turn in the coming weeks.
"By and large, after some downside, we expect a rally again and the bullishness should continue at least until the budget," the note said.
